newsitem.title: UK: Freight rates remain weak, under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Freight rates remain weak, under pressure.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) extended its relentless new decline on Thursday on easier grains fixtures and the buildup of tonnage in the Atlantic. The index fell seven points to 1072 and seems set to re-test the four-year low set on August 8 at 1060 soon, before surplus Panamax tonnage finds chartering for November new crop U.S. grain shipments.
Grains fixtures on Thursday were chiefly of interest for news of Continental chartering that brokers had been awaiting as a benchmark after Monday's US Labor Day weekend.

Continental fixed Aleslevada 54,000/5 heavy grains USGulf/Japan for 18-28 September at $19.25 without combination. The BFI sub-index rate for this route slipped this week below $20 and was quoted on Thursday at $19.821 after $19.971 on Wednesday. Reported fixings on Thursday also included Continental USGulf/Shanghai 50,000/5 58ft spot for about $20 but details were awaited.
Flag Mersinidi fixed 85,000 tonnes heavy grains USGulf/Rotterdam for lumpsum $840,000 fio 12 days for September 20-25 to Dreyfus.

France's grain office ONIC forecast French soft wheat exports to non-EU destinations in the new 1996/97 season may rise to 6.7 million tonnes from a provisional 3.75 million tonnes in 1995/96, trade sources say.
Fixtures in the ore trades on Thursday included Kamikawa Maru 140,000 tonnes ore Tubarao/Rotterdam $5 fio six days 1-10 October to Rohstoffhandel.
Amnong timecharters Neptune Canopus 64,711 dwt fixed GIC delivery Abu Dhabi 12-20 September trip and redelivery Taiwan at $8,000 daily.
BIFFEX futures were also easier again in thin volume with October off 18 at 1195 by 1345 GMT.
